title: finding(core): `register` with `skipFallback: true` still deletes another declaration's bare lazy stub, leaving the bare key claimed by nobody
body:
`Registry.register`'s stub-clearing lines sit OUTSIDE its `meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback` branch, so a registration that explicitly DECLINES the bare key still deletes another declaration's bare lazy stub — and the bare key ends up claimed by nobody at all.

Surfaced while delivering objectui#9821 (PR objectui#9838) and **re-measured at source by the filing seat** on `origin/main` `26ac5036` at 2026-09-18T08:41Z. ⛔ Not carried into that PR: it is a different shape from the card that found it.

## The measurement

`packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts`, `register`:

- `:492` opens `if (meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback) {`
- `:506` `this.components.set(type, { … })` — the bare-key claim, **inside** that branch
- `:511` closes it
- `:515` `this.lazyEntries.delete(fullType);`
- `:516` `this.lazyEntries.delete(type);` — ⭐ **outside**, at function-body level, so it runs unconditionally

⇒ with `skipFallback: true`, `:506` never runs and `:516` runs anyway. The registration declines to claim the bare key, **and takes it away from whoever held it.**

## Reproduction — green named probe, already on PR objectui#9838's branch

`packages/core/src/registry/__tests__/Registry.test.ts`, `skipFallback on the EAGER door does not preserve the stub's bare claim`:

```ts
registry.registerLazy('dashboard', loader, { namespace: 'plugin-dashboard' });
expect(registry.hasLazy('dashboard')).toBe(true);

registry.register('dashboard', () => 'view', { namespace: 'view', skipFallback: true });

// The bare key is now claimed by nobody: the stub was deleted anyway and
// the registration declined to take it.
expect(registry.hasLazy('dashboard')).toBe(false);
expect(registry.get('dashboard')).toBeUndefined();
```

⚠️ That probe **pins today's defective behaviour and says so in its own comment**. It is a pin, ⛔ not a blessing, and it is load-bearing for objectui#9838's warning text: the eager door deliberately does ⛔ **not** prescribe `skipFallback` as the remedy, because this is why it would not settle the contest.

## ⭐ A second face, measured by the filing seat and ⛔ not reported by the delivery

`unregister` at `:530-542` carries the same unconditional pair — and there the asymmetry is visible against its own docblock:

- `:534-536` guards the bare **`components`** key: `if (bare && bare.type === fullType) this.components.delete(type);` — only drops it when it still resolves to this registration
- `:538-539` `this.lazyEntries.delete(fullType); this.lazyEntries.delete(type);` — **no equivalent guard**

Its docblock at `:521-523` says it clears «the bare-name fallback (when the fallback still points at this registration), plus any matching lazy stub».

⚠️ Stated as a reading, ⛔ not as a verdict: whether `:539` is a defect turns on whether «any **matching** lazy stub» means «a stub under either key» or «a stub that belongs to this registration». If the latter, this is the same shape as the `register` half plus a declared≠enforced tell in the docblock. **Whoever triages this should rule that phrase before the fix shape is chosen** — the two readings give two different patches.

## Why this is NOT a duplicate of objectui#9533

objectui#9533 is a stub that is **never cleared** and keeps the bare key. This is the **converse**: a stub that is cleared by a registration which then declines to replace it. Opposite direction, different victim, different fix.

## Dedupe words

- `register` clears the bare lazy stub
- `skipFallback` does not preserve the stub
- unconditional `lazyEntries.delete(type)`
- bare key claimed by nobody
- objectui#9533 unsatisfiable stub
